resteasy_liberty_examples.overview: Real-world examples and complete workflows for common tasks when working with RESTeasy, Open Liberty, Jakarta EE, and MicroProfile codebases.

example.name: adding_new_jaxrs_endpoint
example.scenario: User wants to add a new REST endpoint to an existing JAX-RS resource class

step.details: Search for @Path annotation to locate resource classes

step.action: Read the resource class to understand structure
step.details: Examine existing endpoints, injected services, and patterns
Insert new method with proper annotations before closing brace
Run build command to ensure no compilation errors

key_considerations.consideration: Ensure proper HTTP method annotation (@GET, @POST, etc.)
Use CDI injection for services, not manual instantiation

example.name: debugging_cdi_injection_failure
example.scenario: Application fails to start with CDI deployment error about unsatisfied dependency

step.action: Identify the failing injection point from error message
step.details: Look for "Unsatisfied dependency" or "No bean found" in logs
Search for class name with CDI scope annotations

step.action: Verify bean has proper scope annotation
step.details: Check for @ApplicationScoped, @RequestScoped, etc.
Some beans require explicit discovery configuration

step.action: Look for producer methods if direct bean not found
step.details: Search for @Produces with the bean type
Add missing scope annotation or create producer method

common_causes.cause: Missing scope annotation on bean class
Bean in package not scanned by CDI
Qualifier mismatch between injection point and bean

example.name: adding_osgi_bundle_dependency
example.scenario: Need to add a new package import to an OSGi bundle manifest

step.details: Understand existing imports and structure
Check the exporting bundle's version

step.action: Add the import to the manifest
step.details: Insert in alphabetical order with proper version range
Build the bundle to check for manifest errors

best_practices.practice: Use version ranges like [2.0,3) for major version compatibility
Keep imports alphabetically sorted for maintainability
Document why each import is needed

example.name: implementing_microprofile_health_check
example.scenario: Add a health check to monitor database connectivity

step.details: Implement HealthCheck interface with @Readiness annotation
Use @Inject for DataSource or other services
Test connectivity and return appropriate status
Start server and check /health/ready endpoint

implementation_notes.note: Use @Readiness for dependencies required before accepting traffic
Use @Liveness for detecting deadlocks or unrecoverable states
Include meaningful data in HealthCheckResponse for debugging
Keep health checks fast - they're called frequently

example.name: creating_liberty_feature
example.scenario: Create a new Liberty feature that bundles related functionality

step.details: Define subsystem with symbolic name and dependencies
Include all features this feature depends on
Add all OSGi bundles that make up this feature
Use IBM-API-Package for public APIs
Build feature and test in Liberty server

example.name: adding_microprofile_config_property
example.scenario: Add a new configurable property to a service using MicroProfile Config

step.details: Locate the class that needs configuration
Inject property with name and optional default value
Add comments explaining purpose and valid values
Add to microprofile-config.properties or server.xml

example.name: implementing_jaxrs_exception_mapper
example.scenario: Create exception mapper for consistent error responses

step.details: Implement ExceptionMapper interface with @Provider
Convert exception to appropriate HTTP response
Add to Application.getClasses() if needed
Verify correct status codes and error messages

example.name: debugging_classloader_issue
example.scenario: ClassNotFoundException when trying to use a class from another bundle

step.action: Identify the missing class from stack trace
step.details: Note the full package and class name

step.action: Find which bundle exports the class
step.details: Search for Export-Package in MANIFEST.MF files
Read MANIFEST.MF of bundle that needs the class

step.action: Add missing import if not present
step.details: Add Import-Package with proper version range
Build bundle and test that class is now accessible

troubleshooting_tips.tip: Check if package is exported by any bundle
Look for split packages (same package in multiple bundles)
Check for optional imports that might not be resolved

example.name: adding_microprofile_metrics
example.scenario: Add metrics to track service performance and usage

step.details: Choose key operations to monitor
Add @Counted, @Timed, or @Gauge annotations
For programmatic metric registration
Check /metrics endpoint for new metrics

metric_types.type: Current value that can go up or down (queue size)
Duration and rate of events (method execution time)

pattern.name: read_understand_modify
pattern.description: Always read files first to understand context before modifying

steps.step: Use search_files to locate relevant files
Use read_file to understand current implementation
Use execute_command to verify changes build

pattern.name: trace_dependencies
pattern.description: Follow dependency chains to understand integration

steps.step: Start with injection point or usage
Check OSGi imports/exports if crossing bundles

pattern.name: incremental_changes
pattern.description: Make small, verifiable changes rather than large rewrites

steps.step: Make one logical change at a time
Build and test after each change
